newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong to regulate phone video services.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong to regulate phone video services.

text.p: The Hong Kong government said on Thursday it intended to regulate video-on-demand (VOD) television services,
The service is delivered over domestic telephone lines.
The government said in a statement it intended to create a new category of licences for providers of VOD television services through amendments to the Television Ordinance.
"The bill would provide the necessary legal framework to ensure VOD television services were properly regulated," Chau Tak-hay, Secretary for Broadcasting, Culture and Sport, said.
"The scope of licensing will be limited to services comprising television programmes, including films," he said.
But the bill would not seek to regulate VOD television services originating outside Hong Kong.

"Apart from the difficulty of detecting such services amongst the mass of data flowing over telecommunication systems in Hong Kong, we think that it would be wrong to interfere with people's freedom and privacy of communications," Chau said.
Chau said it might be possible to invite applications for VOD television service licences by end-March 1997 and licences might be issued by mid-1997.
Only two licences might be awarded, he said.
Licensees would be allowed to invest in satellite broadcasting ventures without limits on shareholding. They do not need to obtain prior approval from the Broadcasting Authority.
